# Error compounding over a horizon

[VERIFICATION_FIRST.md](VERIFICATION_FIRST.md) argues that long-horizon agents fail
because per-step errors compound, and that an objective gate is the highest-leverage
place to intervene. [ABLATION.md](ABLATION.md) measures the per-step effect. This page
measures the other half: what that per-step effect compounds to across a horizon —
and it is careful about the difference between re-expressing evidence and adding it.

## The gap this closes

The thesis is about `n` steps. Until now every measurement in this repo was taken at
`n = 1`. That is a real mismatch, and it is the first thing a careful reader should
attack: a 4% per-step effect looks like nothing, and the argument for why it matters
was left as arithmetic the reader had to do themselves.

## Definitions

An **episode** is an ordered sequence of `k` independent subtasks drawn from the
bug-fix corpus (`data/bench/*`). Each subtask is its own repository, its own model
call, and shares no state with the others. The episode is **correct through step k**
only if every one of steps `1..k` truly succeeded, as graded by the ablation's
independent scorer — not by the internal gate.

| condition | gate | repair |
|---|---|---|
| `trust-chain` | off | none — a wrong step is accepted silently and the episode is already lost |
| `verify-chain` | on | up to 3 rounds per step |

Independence is by construction, which buys two things a state-coupled chain would
not. Pairing is exact at **every** `k`, because the attempt drawn at step `k` cannot
depend on what happened earlier, so one measured attempt scores under both conditions.
And the design measures exactly the model
[VERIFICATION_FIRST.md](VERIFICATION_FIRST.md) states — "`n` sequential steps, each
succeeding independently with probability `p`, with no recovery" — rather than a
different, harder-to-attribute one.

## Composition is not new evidence

This is the part that is easy to get wrong, so it is stated plainly.

The **curve** is the compounding model evaluated at the measured per-task `p`. For a
uniformly random ordering, the first `k` steps are a uniformly random `k`-subset, so
`P(correct through k)` is the degree-`k` elementary symmetric polynomial of the
per-step probabilities over `C(n, k)`. It is computed exactly (`horizon.compounding_curve`),
with no sampling noise of its own.

The **evidence** is something else. One repetition of the whole corpus is one
independent episode, so `R` repetitions give exactly `R` episodes. Averaging the curve
over more orderings does not create information: at `R = 3` the paired test at the
terminal step returns `p = 0.50` — *the identical p-value the single-step comparison
returns on the same cells*. That property is pinned by
`tests/test_horizon.py::test_composition_does_not_manufacture_significance`, because a
measurement framework whose headline grows while its evidence does not is exactly the
failure mode this project exists to catch.

So the curve legitimately changes the **effect size** (3.9 pp at one step → 55.6 pp at
seventeen). It does not change the **confidence**. Only more repetitions do.

## Result

Composed from the committed 17-task × 3-rep ablation run (pinned
`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, independent scorer, 0 transient errors); raw data in
[`benchmarks/ablation_report.json`](../benchmarks/ablation_report.json), composed
output in [`benchmarks/horizon_report.md`](../benchmarks/horizon_report.md).

| k | `trust-chain` (95% CI) | `verify-chain` | gap |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 96% (90–100%) | 100% | +3.9 pp |
| 4 | 85% (65–100%) | 100% | +15.2 pp |
| 8 | 71% (42–100%) | 100% | +29.1 pp |
| 12 | 58% (26–100%) | 100% | +41.7 pp |
| 17 | **44% (13–100%)** | **100%** | **+55.6 pp** |

Observed episodes: `trust-chain` 1/3 end-to-end correct, `verify-chain` 3/3. Paired
at the terminal step: discordant 2/0 of 3 · exact McNemar **p = 0.50, not
significant**. The CIs are a task-cluster bootstrap, and they are wide for a concrete
reason: only 2 of 17 subtasks are ever failed by this model, so a resample that misses
both yields a perfect corpus.
<!-- RESULTS:END -->

## Registered prediction

Recorded here **before** any additional repetitions are run, so that the check is a
prediction rather than a description. The git history of this file is the timestamp.

- **Point prediction.** Under `trust-chain`, end-to-end success over all 17 subtasks
  is the product of the measured per-task rates: `1.0^15 × (2/3) × (2/3) = 0.4444`.
  Under `verify-chain`, `1.000`.
- **Stopping rule.** `lha ablate --reps 12`, then regenerate. Twelve is committed in
  advance and is not to be revised after looking at the outcome; at the observed
  discordance rate it is the smallest `R` whose best case clears `p < 0.05`
  (12 episodes, ~7 discordant one-directional → exact McNemar p ≈ 0.016).
- **What would falsify the model.** A measured `trust-chain` terminal rate outside
  roughly 0.25–0.65 at `R = 12` would mean the steps are not behaving independently —
  the composition would then be wrong, not merely imprecise, and the curve would have
  to be withdrawn in favour of an executed multi-step measurement.
- **What is not claimed.** This is a composed curve over independent subtasks. It is
  not an executed 17-step agent run. Those are different claims and the second one is
  still open; see below.

## Still open: the harness has never executed a long plan

Worth stating because the project's name invites the question. The Supervisor's
templates emit **two** steps for `issue_to_pr` and `paper_to_experiment` and one for
`freshness`, so the longest plan this harness has ever actually executed is two steps.
`max_steps=20`, the cross-step checkpoint/resume path, and long-ledger behaviour are
implemented and unit-tested, but they have never been exercised at horizon length by a
real run. Doing that is a separate piece of work from the measurement on this page,
and it is not claimed here.

## Reproduce

```bash
# compose from the committed measured run (no model calls, no network)
uv run lha horizon

# or from your own ablation output
uv run lha --llm claude_cli ablate --reps 12 --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
uv run lha horizon --from-report runs/ablation/ablation_report.json
```

Writes `horizon_report.{md,json}`. The composition logic is deterministic and covered
by `tests/test_horizon.py` (no network), including the property that composing cells
must not manufacture significance.
